where: Main finding 3, CAuSE sentence (claim 18)
problem: The sentence is correctly scoped to what the causal-abstraction search found. But the map already holds bhupatiraju2026stated, which patches activations at the token span of each stated CoT step ("targeted interchange intervention on self-generated reasoning") and scores whether the answer flips to the predicted target. That is closer to treating written steps as high-level variables than CAuSE is, although it is an operational metric (definitions.csv rows #4 and #7, kinds operational and criterion), not a definition.
fix: Optionally add after the CAuSE sentence: "Within the map, [Bhupatiraju & Nyaupane 2026](./#p=bhupatiraju2026stated) apply targeted interchange interventions at the tokens of each stated step, but as a metric, not as a definition."

where: Structural causal models, What it cannot express: "Agents' beliefs and intentions need the game extension below, and a monitor's computational limits need the information-theoretic family."
problem: Overstated and inconsistent with the page's own table, which lists "Structural causal models with an epistemic state: intention ([Halpern & Kleiman-Weiner 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05903))". search_agency_honesty.json records that paper's intention definitions (Defs. 4.1, 4.4, 4.8) in "Halpern-Pearl structural causal models with an epistemic state (probability over causal models and a utility)". Only belief, and belief, intention and deception together, need the game extension.
fix: Intention needs an epistemic state over causal models ([Halpern & Kleiman-Weiner 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05903)), belief and deception need the game extension below, and a monitor's computational limits need the information-theoretic family.

where: Structural causal models, Concepts covered: "with mediation, faithfulness as complete mediation by the CoT and, as a proposed reading, post-hoc rationalization as a null indirect effect."
problem: Only the second half is labeled as a proposal. No formal.csv row in this family defines CoT faithfulness as complete mediation by the CoT (Pearl 2001 defines mediation in general, and Remark 53 of Geiger et al. concerns hidden vectors, not a CoT). The page's Conjectures paragraph proposes this same reading (a null natural direct effect of the instruction on the answer, with the CoT as mediator) alongside the post-hoc rationalization reading.
fix: with mediation, and as proposed readings, faithfulness as complete mediation by the CoT and post-hoc rationalization as a null indirect effect.

where: Claim 84 (Observer-relative information, What it defines)
problem: The claim is supported, but "require only that ... but that ..." can read as if Kim & Lee's checkability were weaker overall. It relaxes completeness, but its soundness quantifies over every proof ($\forall z'\in\mathcal Z$), whereas Kirchner et al. quantify over provers from the same family ($\forall\pi'\in\mathcal H$) (definitions.csv kim2026mitigating#2, kirchner2024proververifier#3).
fix: Optional rewording of the second half: "while [Kim & Lee 2026](./#p=kim2026mitigating) require only that the verifier accept the prover's correct answers, and that "there exists no adversarial proof that can trick the verifier into accepting an incorrect answer", over every proof rather than over provers from one family."

where: Claim 114 (What is missing, The vacuity of unrestricted abstraction)
